title: AWS Launches Strands Box to Control Autonomous AI Agents With Open-Source Sandbox
key_facts: AWS released Strands Box, an open-source sandbox for AI agents, using OS-level isolation.
It uses the Dogwood Local Engine so that rules can consider what an agent has already done, not only what it wants to do.
Example rule: an agent may post to Slack no more than three times every ten minutes.
Box can control when an agent may do a Git push or cap costly API calls.
It includes Strands Shell and Monty for Python so shell and Python actions pass through the same policy engine.
It is on GitHub now for macOS only; Linux is in development and Windows 'on our radar', no release dates.
AWS engineer Marc Brooker says developers remain responsible for deciding what access to grant and where human review is needed.
quote_evidence: “Agents increasingly run in ‘YOLO mode,’ approving every action without human review,” the AWS team explained in its announcement.
“Developers remain responsible for deciding what access to grant and where human review is needed,” Brooker added
why_it_matters_hint: Gives developers rule-based limits on autonomous agents, without relying on the agent to obey.
